scenario:
PROJECT NO. 1 – A PROPOSED BEACH HOUSE

Statement of the problem: A 67-year-old man plans to build his retirement beach house on his two-hectare property in El Nido, a forested site with a natural beachfront and an existing jetty. The house is primarily for his personal use, but his teenage grandchildren will visit often, so the design must balance privacy, accessibility and family interaction, respond to an elderly user, and make the most of the natural beauty, environmental conditions and coastal character of the site.

Site features: The property gently slopes about 2% toward the west, where the beachfront and jetty are. The western edge was previously shaved down for the jetty. The eastern side is the highest point and connects directly to the access road (RROW). The surroundings are forested. The development consists of three detached roofed pods:

• POD 2, the Semi-Public Pod – Dining and Kitchen; the central hub and transition between private and public zones.
• POD 3, the Public/Leisure Pod – Infinity Pool, Pool Deck, Lanai, Bar, Outdoor Living Area and a dance area; at the lowest portion facing the beachfront, with direct access to the jetty.
A six-car garage is required, and service items such as the water pump and septic tank must be placed safely, accessibly and in compliance with environmental rules.

q: Geotechnical results show medium-dense coastal sand, a high groundwater table, and seasonal scouring along the beachfront. The villa is a low-rise structure with modest column loads, but the site is prone to differential settlement due to varying sand compaction between the lanai, living area, and private pod. The owner also requires an economical foundation system that will resist scour, uplift, and uneven settlement. Which foundation type is MOST appropriate?
o: Stiffener mat (raft) foundation to distribute loads across the entire footprint and resist scout and differential settlement
Driven piles to reach deeper bearing strata and eliminate settlement concerns
Isolated footings tied with grade beams to minimize cost while supporting individual column loads on medium-dense sand
Combined footings with grade beams to reduce concrete volume and isolate structural zones
n: A stiffened mat spreads the light loads over the whole footprint, so differential settlement on variable sand is small. Its perimeter can be deepened against scour, and it costs less than piles. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering; FEMA P-55 (Coastal Construction Manual).

q: The rooftop bar offers full dining service, requiring a compact but efficient kitchen layout. To prevent staff flashing, ensure smooth workflow, and maintain high-volume service, what is the best kitchen design approach?

A linear workflow with separated stations arranged for one-directional movement
A central island layout where staff circulate around the island

As the architect, you must recommend the single most effective construction solution to prevent structure-borne vibration and impact noise from transmitting into the offices below. Which solution best addresses the problem?
o: Construct a Floating Floor System beneath the illuminated dance floor to isolate impact and low-frequency vibration from the structural slab.
Add rubber pads under the DJ booth and subwoofers to reduce localized equipment vibration.
Apply sound-absorbing wall panels around the dance floor to reduce reflected noise.
